name: Kobold
summary: In Azeroth's mines and caverns, kobolds guard the candles fixed to their heads. Small and rat-like, they dig in the dark and defend their tunnels in numbers.

sections.title: Miners of the Dark
sections.body: Kobolds stand barely four feet tall. Filthy scavengers, they spend their lives delving underground. Their low-light vision fails in the deepest shafts, so each kobold fixes a crude candle to its head. Alone, one is cowardly when cornered. Yet kobolds breed in massive numbers and work with relentless energy. When agitated, their rat-like tails whip as they rush intruders in frantic swarms. They wield heavy iron mining picks and beat foes to death with them.

sections.title: You No Take Candle!
sections.body: Kobolds fear pitch-black tunnels with a deep, primal terror. To them, a candle is more than light. Its flame shields them from a darkness they believe will consume them.

sections.title: Subterranean Pests of the Kingdoms
sections.body:
Across the Eastern Kingdoms, kobolds often overrun working mines. In Elwynn Forest, a clan displaced from the Redridge Mountains seized the Echo Ridge, Fargodeep, and Jasperlode mines. Riverpaw gnolls and the Defias Brotherhood helped drive them there. In Loch Modan, the Tunnel Rat clan seized the Silver Stream Mine from the dwarven Miners' League.

Kobolds also plague industrial digs in Kalimdor. They labor for the Venture Company in Stonetalon and uncover strange minerals in Thousand Needles.

faq.q: Why do kobolds care so much about their candles?
faq.answer: Kobolds feel deep, paralyzing terror at complete darkness. Their folklore treats it as a predator that snuffs out life and swallows miners whole. They guard their candles as their only defense.
Kobolds' true origins are unknown. They have dwelt in tunnels and caverns beneath Azeroth for as long as anyone remembers, wherever earth can be dug.

faq.q: Are kobolds allied with the Defias Brotherhood?
faq.answer: Kobolds were not willing partners of the Defias Brotherhood. In Elwynn Forest and Westfall, Riverpaw gnolls largely bullied and enslaved them. The Defias hired those gnolls to disrupt mining and secure mineral wealth.

faq.q: How do kobolds choose their leaders?
faq.answer: Kobolds have no single ruler. Each clan answers to its own bosses, including taskmasters who drive the diggers to work in the mines they claim.

faq.q: Are kobolds found in Kalimdor as well as the Eastern Kingdoms?
faq.answer: Yes. Kobolds infested the underground caverns beneath Orgrimmar during the city's founding. They also work in the Venture Company's Windshear Mine in the Stonetalon Mountains and burrow throughout Thousand Needles.
Little is recorded about kobold diets. They are filthy scavengers who live on whatever they find in and around their tunnels.

angles.text: As a miner in human or dwarven lands, you will inevitably encounter kobold infestations. Kobolds gravitate toward rich veins of copper, tin, and silver.
For the Kingdom of Stormwind, kobolds are a constant economic headache. They have overrun vital local operations at Fargodeep, Jasperlode, and Echo Ridge.
As a dwarf, you know the Miners' League regularly employs adventurers to clear Tunnel Rat kobolds from mountain digs like the Silver Stream Mine in Loch Modan.
As a member of the Horde, you know kobold warrens beneath the dry earth caused chaos during Orgrimmar's founding. Clans like the Gravelsnouts still harass frontier outposts in Kalimdor.
